The landscape of Ann Arbor consists of hills and valleys, with the terrain becoming steeper near the [Huron River](/wiki/Huron_River "Huron River"). The work force in Macau is mainly composed of manufacturing; construction; wholesale and retail; hotels and restaurants; financial services, real estate, and other business activities; public administration and other personal and social services, including gaming; transport, storage and communications. Due to the double-digit economic growth in recent years, the [unemployment rate](/wiki/Unemployment_rate "Unemployment rate") dropped from the record high 6.8% in 2000 to 3.1% in Qtr 3, 2007.[[55]](#cite_note-laborstat-57)

With the opening of several casino resorts and other major constructions underway, it is reported that many sectors, especially the construction sector, experience a shortage of labour. The government responds by importing labour from other neighboring regions, including mainland China, Hong Kong, the [Philippines](/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") and [India](/wiki/India "India"). Currently the number of imported labours stands at a record high of 75,391 (Q2 2007), representing more than a quarter of the labour force in Macau.[[56]](#cite_note-pstat-58)[[57]](#cite_note-laborstat2-59) Some local workers complain about the lack of jobs due to the influx of cheap imported labour. Some also claim that the problem of illegal labour is severe.[[58]](#cite_note-60) Another concern is the widening of income inequality in the region: Macau's [Gini coefficient](/wiki/Gini_coefficient "Gini coefficient"), a popular measure of income inequality where a low value indicates a more equal income distribution, rises from 0.43 in 1998 to 0.48 in 2006. It is higher than those of other neighboring regions, such as mainland China (0.447), [South Korea](/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea") (0.316) and [Singapore](/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") (0.425).[[59]](#cite_note-61)

Uranus orbits the Sun once every 84 years. As viewed against the background of stars, since being discovered in 1781,[[67]](#cite_note-76) the planet has returned to the point of its discovery northeast of the binary star [Zeta Tauri](/wiki/Zeta_Tauri "Zeta Tauri") twice—in March 1865 and March 1949—and will return to this location again in April 2033.[[68]](#cite_note-77)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Uranus_right_ascension.png/500px-Uranus_right_ascension.png)](/wiki/File:Uranus_right_ascension.png)

Right ascension of Uranus in two 2-year intervals, 84 years apart

Because the period is very close to 84 years, its apparent position in the stars is very close to what it was exactly 84 years earlier (see graph). The [retrograde motion](/wiki/Retrograde_motion "Retrograde motion") of Uranus brings it back each year to approximately the most easterly position it had the previous year.

Its average distance from the Sun is roughly 20 [AU](/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit") (3 [billion](/wiki/1000000000_(number) "1000000000 (number)") [km](/wiki/Kilometre "Kilometre"); 2 billion [mi](/wiki/Mile "Mile")). The difference between its minimum and maximum distance from the Sun is 1.8 AU, larger than that of any other planet, though not as large as that of dwarf planet [Pluto](/wiki/Pluto "Pluto").[[69]](#cite_note-AA-78) The intensity of sunlight varies inversely with the square of the distance—on Uranus (at about 20 times the distance from the Sun compared to Earth), it is about 1/400 the intensity of light on Earth.[[70]](#cite_note-79)
